title: How Crews Found the 49th Parallel by the Stars #shorts
summary: From 1872 to 1875 survey crews fixed the 49th parallel by astronomy about every 32 km; west of the Rockies, mountains deflected plumb lines and British and American marks differed.
tags: why is the us canada border straight
sources: The 49th parallel east of the Rockies was originally surveyed during the years 1872 to 1875; latitude determined by astronomic observations at about 32-kilometre (20-mile) intervals; the prairie section resurveyed, mapped and monumented 1909-1912 (International Boundary Commission, Section E, Gulf of Georgia to the Northwesternmost Point of Lake of the Woods): https://internationalboundarycommission.org/en/maps-coordinates/maps/section-e.php

HistoryLink Essay 5199 (Kit Oldham, 2003): local land masses create gravitational pulls that deflect plumb lines and skewed the latitude readings; marked points were joined by straight lines while a parallel is curved; three defendants charged after searches at border crossings argued their alleged crimes occurred north of the parallel: https://www.historylink.org/File/5199

The first instance of a boundary drawn first on paper then traced on the ground; latitude determined with the zenith telescope (Talcott method) (American Society of Civil Engineers, Historic Civil Engineering Landmark: United States-Canadian Boundary Survey): https://www.asce.org/about-civil-engineering/history-and-heritage/historic-landmarks/united-states-canadian-boundary-survey

Map data: Natural Earth (public domain) https://www.naturalearthdata.com and US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain) https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/carto-boundary-file.html

scenes.narration: From {1872|eighteen seventy-two} to {1875|eighteen seventy-five}, crews fixed the {49th|forty-ninth} parallel by the stars, about every {32 km|thirty-two kilometres}.
On the prairie, they marked it with mounds of earth and sod, and later iron posts.
West of the Rockies, British and American marks came out up to {860 feet|eight hundred and sixty feet} apart.

data.source: State v. Norman (Wash. 2002), citing the 1861 survey

scenes.narration: The culprit: mountains. Their mass tugs on a plumb line and skews the star reading.
